Design board · 22 November 2026 · not a handoff, nothing here is in the app

The whole app, in the approved look

Every route of the app, redrawn with what you approved today: the ink top, the white sheet, lifted cards, their dark version, and the footer where the bar is the button. 173 phones cover 53 routes. The words, the figures and the order of things on each screen are the app’s; only the chrome and the surfaces changed. Approve a screen, or say what to change on it. Code changes wait for your approval here.

The headerThe top of an ink screen, in white type. A back chevron and the title; a step or a status at the right. Tonight keeps its pot up there.
The sheet and the cardsOne white sheet rises over the ink. Groups are white cards on one soft shadow. Nothing grey sits under content; inputs are outlined.
The bar is the buttonA screen’s one primary action is the ink bar at the bottom, words straight on it. Faint when it is not available yet. Other actions stay in the content, outlined or as quiet text.
SheetsKeep their grabber and close. A sheet that ends in Save or Add ends in the same bar. Behind each one is the screen it opened from, dimmed.
Kept from Fresh DeckNames only, nothing points, red belongs to chips and to hearts and diamonds, no green fills.
Not yet seen on a phoneThese are 330-point mock phones. Use the switch below to see every one of them dark.

Building it

The new look is being written into the app in parts, in this order: what has the fewest open questions goes first. A built screen is shown beside its drawing — the right-hand phone is the app itself, photographed at 393 × 852 off its web build — and has its own Approve / Needs work. Plan as of 24 November 2026.

  1. 0 Built

    The look underneath

    Everything every screen stands on, so each later part is content only.

    • Colours: the kit’s palette for light and dark, the approved dark sheet and footer (tokens.ts)
    • Two faces shipped with the app: Libre Franklin for titles, the bar and every money figure; Inter for the rest
    • Pushed screens: the ink top with a bare back chevron, the white sheet rising over it
    • Sheets: 24-point corners, grabber, round close, a back circle for a later step
    • The bar: one action, two equal halves, blocked, a line above, a sub-line
    • Cards on the shorter shadow, rows with no chevrons, section labels, lifted chips (C), presets, the keypad as a grid
    • The approved drawings, exported from the icon board into the app
    • Screens not yet in their part already wear the ink top, the new sheet, the colours and the faces; their primary button stays a filled button in the content until their part moves it to the bar.
    • The muted-most grey stays at the app’s readable value rather than the kit’s #9AA2B1, which measures 2.5:1 on white against the 4.5 floor the checks hold.
    • A title never scrolls away any more: on the ink it would be white on the white sheet. My stats and Players used to let it.

To review

Every screen without your approval, in the app’s order. A screen you approve moves down to Approved once you are not typing.

This round: the games-and-hours line on My stats

Three ways to set “6 games · 25 h” beside the month’s result, on the fuller book. Everything else on the screen is as before; the break-even night has lost its $0.

This round: Add players, one line per player

The version you picked to see further: the buy-in written like a seat’s, Add as a small lifted chip. Every state the sheet has: at rest, a buy-in being typed, searching, a search with no match, a new name typed, and a name already at the table. Words are the app’s.

Home, Tonight and the settled night

The three places the approved look was reviewed on, redrawn with the kit, plus Tonight’s drawer open and the sheet behind Rebuy.

Getting in

Signing in by emailed link, naming the account, choosing or starting a group, and an invite seen from both ends.

Opening a game

New session is one sheet: the game in a line, the seating as its body, and every step behind it (game details, a rule, the currency, someone new, the membership gate) replacing its content.

During the game

What the host opens from Tonight while the game runs: a player’s card, the amount keypad, seating someone new, correcting an entry, and the tools chooser.

Running the game

Who records the night: passing it to a person, what every other phone reads on Tonight, watching by link, and reviewing what another phone recorded.

The bill

What the night spent and how it is shared: the bill, a spend, one person’s share set by hand, and the two small sheets the count-up opens, End time and Rounding.

Ending the night: count and deductions

Steps 1 and 2 of the three that close a night: every stack is counted until the money adds up, then the group’s rules take their shares before anyone is told who pays whom.

Ending the night: who pays whom

The transfers that close the session, the same step when the count is off, the settled night read two more ways, and the payments ticked off afterwards.

Sessions, stats and the group

Home’s first three tiles: the list of nights, where a player stands over a stretch, and the roster with one member’s sheet.

Settings and money rules

The group’s settings, the money rules a night starts from and runs under, the rule editor, the table rules, and deleting an account.

Your plan

Changing a membership from Settings, outside the gate on opening a game: what you are on, moving up, moving down, stopping, and what happens when a plan runs out. New screens; draft words throughout.

Poker tools

The calculator and its run-out picture, the rulings library and one ruling, and the game boosters: tools beside the game, none of which touch the ledger.

Approved

Screens you have approved, by section.
